import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_4.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV into a dataframe
# All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
# ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# So we can safely concatenate (union) them.
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in order
    df = df[['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# According to the examples, the 'Winner' column contains string values "NO" or possibly "YES"
# We keep it as is.

# The 'Year' column format is like "2010 (83rd)" which matches target examples, so no change needed.

# The 'Movie' column sometimes contains strings with embedded braces, e.g. "Lost in Translation {'Bob Harris'}"
# The target examples keep this format, so no change needed.

# The 'Category', 'Nominee' columns are strings and appear consistent.

# Final dataframe matches the target schema exactly.

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
